discovery: Establishing molecular astrophysics: the physical and chemical processes that govern interstellar clouds and star- and planet-forming regions

nominees.name: Alexander G. G. M. Tielens
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, USA, and Leiden Observatory, Netherlands

subfield: Astrophysics / astrochemistry and star and planet formation
motivation: The nominees turned interstellar molecules into quantitative probes of the physics of cosmic origins. Herbst established gas-phase ion-molecule and grain-surface reaction networks that explain the chemical complexity of cold clouds. Tielens developed the theory of photodissociation regions and of interstellar dust and ice processing, linking radiation fields, heating and cooling to observed spectra. Van Dishoeck combined laboratory molecular physics, photodissociation theory and observations with ISO, Spitzer, Herschel, ALMA and JWST. She showed how water, ices and organic molecules evolve from collapsing clouds into protoplanetary disks. Together they built the framework now used to measure temperatures, densities, ionization and timescales in regions where stars and planets form. Their work explains how the ingredients of planetary systems, including our own, are made and inherited. It turned spectroscopy of molecules into a precision tool of astrophysics.
